text:
Name: Surface-feeding Duck - Subfamily Anatienae
Montana resident in: Spring, summer, fall, winter
Habitat: Lakes, ponds, rivers, marshes, grainfields, irrigated lands, and prairies.
Foods: Pondweed (1), Bulrush (1), spikerush (1), muskgrass (1), corn (1), sedge (1), wheat and algae.
Miscellaneous: Prized by sportsmen.
Name: Diving Ducks - Subfamily Aythyinae
Montana resident in: Spring, summer, fall, winter
Habitat: Lakes, marshes and rivers.
Foods: Pondweed (1), bulrush, algae, saltgrass, sedge, waterweed, aquatic insects (adult and larvae) crusteaceans, mollusks and fish.
Miscellaneous: Goldeneye and bufflehead feed mostly on animal life.
Name: Stiff-tailed Ducks - Subfamily Oxyurinae
Montana resident in: Spring, summer, fall, winter.
Habitat: Lakes, marshes and ponds.
Foods: Pondweed, bulrush, sedge, aquatic grasses, aquatic insects,
mollusks and crustaceans.
Miscellaneous: The ruddy duck, <u>Oxyura jamaicensis</u> is the only species of this subfamily found in Montana.
Name: Mergansers - Subfamily merginae
Montana resident in: Spring, summer, fall, winter.
Habitat: Wooded lakes, lakes, ponds and rivers.
Foods: Fish (major diet), crayfish, shrimps, frogs, insects and mollusks.
Miscellaneous: Fish eating habits cause some damage to game fish populations.
Name: American Vultures - Family cathartidae
Montana resident in: Spring, summer, fall, winter.
Habitat: Usually seen airborne, perched, or feeding on ground.
Foods: Carrion.
Miscellaneous: Turkey vulture, <u>Cathartes</u> <u>aura</u> is only Montana species, very beneficial.
Name: Bird Hawks - Subfamily Accipitrinae
Montana resident in: Spring, summer, fall, winter.
Habitat: Forests, river gourges and wooded area.
Foods: Mostly other birds including domestic fowl and game birds, some rodents.
Miscellaneous: All members are of Genus Accipiter. Habit or preying on important birds has given this group a bad reputation.
Name: Buzzard Hawks - Subfamily Buteoninae
Montana resident in: Spring, summer, fall, winter.
Habitat: Open country, woodlands, mountains, deserts.
Foods: Rodents, rabbits, snakes, lizards and small birds. Swamsons feed on insects commonly.
Miscellaneous: Swainsons migrates south in winter. Mostly beneficial habits however redtailed may become problem with poultry.
